reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a widely debunked myth. Modern neuroscience has proven that humans use virtually all parts of their brains throughout the day. Neuroimaging technologies, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) scans, consistently show that even during sleep, nearly all areas of the brain exhibit some level of activity. Furthermore, evolutionary biology and medical science support this: brain tissue is metabolically expensive to maintain, and any unused or "dormant" brain regions would quickly atrophy (degenerate) or be weeded out by natural selection. Damage to almost any area of the brain results in significant functional deficits, confirming that there are no vast, untapped reservoirs of the brain.
